speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If the Donor loses mental capacity, the LPA allows the Donee to decide on the Donor's personal welfare, property and other affairs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Previously, LPAs were made using hard copy forms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In 2021, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) amended the MCA to digitalise the LPA process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This provided more convenience and facilitated an uptake in the number of LPAs created.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The online LPA system was rolled out on 14 November 2022.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The LPA is a legal document which confers powers enabling a Donee to decide on the Donor's personal welfare, property and other affairs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In most cases, the property, such as a Housing and Development Board (HDB) flat, a private condominium apartment or a landed property, is registered under the Land Titles Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To transfer ownership of such a property, there is no need for a deed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, for property not registered under the Land Titles Act, transfer of ownership must be made by way of a deed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Hence, an LPA is executed as a deed, so that irrespective of the type of property, the Donee has the power to make the necessary transactions for the benefit of the Donor.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Prior to the electronic LPAs, the hard copy form contained a statement in the signature box where the Donor physically signs, that the LPA is "signed (or marked) and delivered as a deed by Donor".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Section 12A(1)(a) of the MCA is intended to replicate this for electronic LPAs and specifies that the electronic record must clearly state on its face that it is intended to be a deed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Unfortunately, the electronic LPA, unlike the hard copy form, did not contain this required statement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Two Members of the House have also filed Parliamentary Questions on the matter and I would like to take the opportunity to address them here.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, we apologise for this omission and for any inconvenience this may have caused.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since 5 January this year, the electronic LPA has been revised to include this statement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Next, let me touch on the implications of the omission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Hard copy LPAs, on the other hand, were not affected by this omission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Till date, MSF is not aware of any actual harm suffered by Donees or Donors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many of the Donors that made the LPAs continue to have mental capacity, and so, there is no need yet for the Donees to act on their behalf.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is possible that some Donees have begun to exercise the powers in some of the affected electronic LPAs, but we are not aware of any challenge to the exercise of those powers by third parties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This Bill will remove any future potential complications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Lastly, on the process by which the electronic LPA form was approved for deployment, MSF had an internal proofreading and vetting process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The forms were prepared by the staff of the Office of the Public Guardian and was vetted by the Public Guardian, as well as by a separate Legal Unit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Unfortunately, no system of process checks can be 100% accurate, as this case shows.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In fact, the electronic LPA forms go through various parties, including certificate issuers who are people familiar with the hard copy forms, such as lawyers or doctors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Despite this, it took nearly a year before a member of the public noticed the difference and wrote in to enquire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our key consideration was to ensure certainty of the validity of the LPAs which the Donors had made, so that the Donors would not have to take steps to re-make their LPAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our intent is to validate all affected electronic LPAs, provided they comply with all other legal requirements for the making of an LPA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Subsection (3) additionally provides that no legal proceedings may be instituted on or after 6 March 2024 over the validity of these LPAs by reason of the instruments, or forms, used in the making of the LPA not being in accordance with section 12A(1)(a).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With this amendment, the uncertainty over the validity of all affected electronic LPAs will be removed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Again, we apologise for the omission and assure affected Donors that they do not need to re-make their LPAs.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I was concerned to learn about the omission of the sentence in the LPA expressly stating that it is intended to be a deed.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: All affected LPA documents will be validated when this section passes into law and comes into force.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With this change, affected Donors do not need to remake their LPAs and they would not need to take any action.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   May I seek clarification regarding the treatment of the electronic LPAs during interim period before the Bill becomes law?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How are affected parties be protected and whether there have been any cases of disgruntled family members of affected donors contesting the validity of the LPAs and requesting new donees to be appointed?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What measures are being taken to ensure that such omissions do not occur in the future, both in terms of electronic LPAs and other related documents?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In addition, as I had shared in the House before, would the Ministry consider reviewing and enhancing the safeguards for Donors to prevent potential financial exploitation?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If Donees siphon away or spend the Donors' monies carelessly, other family members or our national coffers will have to pay for the care of the Donors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Presently, these cases of opportunistic Donees are very few, but their numbers are likely to increase as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For clients who have lost their mental capacity, medical diagnoses need to be submitted when applying for a Court order to appoint a pro bono Donee.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is the average duration required to retrieve such medical records?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These 87,000 LPAs were certified between 14 November 2022 and 4 January 2024.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The omission is in respect of the statutory requirement pursuant to section 12A(1)(a) of the Mental Capacity Act 2008, for an LPA to state expressly that it is intended to be a deed by the Donor.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The primary lesson in every such episode, is how we all can be better and actually take all the steps to be better.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I appreciate that the OPG that they have been transparent in accounting for its mistake and swift in remedying the potential consequences.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The electronic LPA was a laudable initiative and which has benefited numerous Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In our mission to be and do better, I seek several clarifications over the issue.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While this Bill negates the need for any remedial actions on the Donors' part, Donees could understandably be anxious and uncertain about the ramifications stemming from the error, coupled with the fact that the LPA Donor is no longer able to amend his or her LPA.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Next, has the OPG directly notified all affected parties?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This would include but not necessarily be limited to the Donors and Donees but, perhaps, also the lawyers who may have assisted in the Donor's e-submissions of the affected LPAs.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Additionally, how has the OPG, at the organisational level; as well as MSF, at the Ministry level, been assisting and supporting those affected?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As part of its rectification efforts and aside from this Bill, has or will the OPG and MSF consider enlisting the assistance of the members of the legal profession and other appropriate personnel?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our community is our greatest and most valuable resource and we have many who stand ready to volunteer their assistance.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It would also be understandable for the affected Donors and/or Donees to want to relook at the affected LPAs.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this regard, will the OPG consider permitting them to do so and if they choose to do so, also allow for them to make amendments at no charge?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Lastly, LPA Donors and Donees have been able to apply for a hard copy and certified true copy of the LPA through the OPG's portal.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To assure those affected beyond a shadow of a doubt, would the Minister please confirm that the copies of the LPA ,which have been issued by the OPG, remain valid following the passage of this Bill and that there will be no need for any re-application or re-issuance?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It ensures that our wishes are respected, even if we can no longer express them ourselves.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I understand that retrospective action has been taken, I seek some clarifications.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, why was this oversight not identified earlier?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What drafting and vetting processes failed in transporting the physical LPA to the online version?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If there is any legal cost involved resultantly, which party will bear the costs?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moving forward, how does the Ministry plan to inform LPA Donors about the corrective changes made?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will they receive a hard copy letter outlining the necessary information?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: More importantly, what measures will be put in place to prevent similar situations from happening in the future?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be a system in place to check and ensure all essential clauses are included in future e-documents prepared by the Government?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Government should not allow such concerns to cast a shadow of doubt over the overall benefits of adopting a digital system for Government services.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Ensuring public trust and confidence in these systems require transparency and proactive measures to prevent future issues.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us continue to embrace technological advancements while safeguarding the legal validity and effectiveness of the use of electronic documents in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is vitally important as we continue to encourage Singaporeans to plan for end-of-life issues early.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Affected Donors do not need to re-make their LPAs and no action is required on their part.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To date, MSF has not received any requests for electronic LPAs to be re-made.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Several questions have been raised by Members on the impact to those affected, as well as the support provided.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Ms Hany Soh asked about how many of the 87,000 affected LPA Donors have since become mentally incapacitated and if Certified True Copies of electronic LPAs that have been issued would have to be re-issued.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Currently, there is no requirement for the Donee to inform the OPG when the Donor loses mental capacity or when an LPA is used.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Nonetheless, according to our records, the vast majority of the affected LPAs have not yet been shared with third parties.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Bill, once it comes into effect, will remove any uncertainty over the validity of these LPAs on the basis of the omitted statement.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In addition, third parties who have transacted with Donees based on a Certified True Copy of the electronic LPA may continue to rely on these documents for the transaction.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: However, we recommend that third parties request for the online registered LPA rather than a Certified True Copy, to ensure that they obtain the most updated version.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Ms Hany Soh and Mr Don Wee also asked how affected parties will be supported and protected in the interim and if there have been challenges made against the affected LPAs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Since the issue was made public, MSF has not been made aware of any such challenges being brought against the affected electronic LPAs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Ms Hany Soh, Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if there will be notice given to affected Donors, to inform them that their LPAs will now be recognised as valid.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As no action is required by these Donors, we will not send individual notices.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Instead, a note will be affixed to the registration page of affected electronic LPAs to point to the retroactive validating provision, when the Bill comes into effect.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Queries were also raised by Members on measures to strengthen our processes, and on enhancing the LPA and deputyship regimes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Ms Hany Soh, Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about possible measures that can be taken to ensure such an incident does not happen again, including enlisting the assistance of the legal profession.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: While no system of checks can be a 100% foolproof, MSF will continue to proof-read and vet all documents as thoroughly and as meticulously as possible.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will perform a final vetting of all documents prior to a system launch, to ensure compliance with operational as well as legal requirements.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Don Wee has also raised several other queries relating to the LPA and deputyship regime.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: On the safeguards to prevent the financial exploitation of Donors, the Mental Capacity Act contains several provisions to address potential cases of financial exploitation.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For instance, if the court is satisfied that fraud or undue pressure was used to induce a Donor to execute an LPA, the court may direct that the LPA be not registered or revoked, amongst other things.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Public Guardian may also investigate any alleged contravention of the Act and may interview a Donor to ascertain whether he or she had executed an LPA under fraud or undue pressure.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In addition, financial exploitation of Donors may also amount to criminal offences, such as under the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: If any person suspects or believes that a person who lacks mental capacity is being financially exploited, they may report this to the Public Guardian and the Police.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Office of the Public Guardian promptly looks into such reports and works closely with the relevant agencies such as banks to take swift action and minimise harm done to the person who lacks mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In addition, the Public Guardian may also apply to the court to suspend or revoke the LPA or place the Donee or Deputy under closer supervision.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Today, before an application for deputyship can be made, the individual intending to apply for deputyship will have to obtain a medical report from a doctor certifying the individual’s lack of mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: This medical report has to be dated no earlier than six months before the deputyship application, which ensures that the information provided is current.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: An assessment of mental capacity assesses an individual’s ability to take in information presented and demonstrate sufficient reasoning in order to make informed decisions.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As mental capacity may fluctuate over time, a proper assessment of the current mental capacity of an individual cannot rely on historical health information in medical records such as the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR).

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The simplified deputyship application typically takes four to six weeks, which is faster than the standard deputyship applications.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will continue to review how we can improve the process while ensuring sufficient safeguards against potential fraud or undue pressure.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Don Wee has also asked about the LPA take-up rates.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Indeed, making an LPA is an important step in planning ahead for ourselves and our loved ones.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: With an LPA in place, we can be better assured that our loved ones are empowered to support us and manage our affairs, should we lose our mental capacity.
